title: The 10 Best Floor Jacks
subtitle: 2-ton to 3-ton hydraulic floor jacks for cars, SUVs and trucks, low-profile and high-lift, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A floor jack lifts one corner or end of a vehicle so you can set jack stands under it. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a dual-piston pump for faster lifting, a low entry height, at least 18 inches of lift, 3-ton capacity and a stated ANSI/ASME safety standard). Match the jack to the vehicle: low-profile jacks slide under sports cars and sedans, high-lift jacks reach SUVs and trucks. They run from about $46 for DNA Motoring's 2-ton to $170 for Jack Boss's aluminum 3-ton. Never work under a car held only by a jack.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: AV Steel Low Profile Floor Jack 3 Ton (6600 lbs), Dual Pistons Quick Lift Pump, 3-1/8" to 19-7/8" (AV-300102F)
products.verdict: The widest lift range here: a 3-1/8-inch entry that slides under low cars and a 19-7/8-inch top that reaches SUVs, with a dual-piston pump, a 3-ton rating and the ANSI/ASME PASE standard.
products.best_for: One jack for both the sports car and the SUV.
products.skip_if: You only work on one sedan; a 2.5-ton jack costs half as much.

products.name: DNA Motoring TOOLS-00234 Low Profile Hydraulic Trolley Service/Floor Jack, 2 Ton (4000 lbs), 5.1"-13"
products.verdict: The best-selling and cheapest floor jack here: a 2-ton steel trolley jack with an overload valve and swivel casters, enough for tire changes and brakes on a car.
products.best_for: Tire swaps and brake jobs on a sedan.
products.skip_if: You have an SUV or truck; 13 inches of lift won't get the wheels off the ground.
cons: No warranty or safety standard listed

products.name: VEVOR 2.5 Ton Low Profile Heavy-Duty Steel Racing Floor Jack (S385)
products.verdict: A low-profile 2.5-ton jack that slides under lowered cars at 3.35 inches, with a 360-degree saddle, a foam handle bumper and CE and ASME PALD certifications, for under $60.
products.skip_if: You need to lift an SUV; it tops out under 15 inches.

products.name: BIG RED Hydraulic Trolley Service/Floor Jack with Extra Saddle (SUVs and Extended Height Trucks), 3 Ton (T83006)
products.verdict: The most-reviewed jack here and the highest lift: an extra-long saddle neck reaches 20-7/8 inches for trucks and SUVs, with a 3-ton rating for about $90.
products.skip_if: You have a low car; the 5-7/8-inch entry won't fit under it.
cons: Listing showed only 15 left in stock

products.name: Maxority 3-Ton (6600lbs) Low Profile Hydraulic Heavy-Duty Steel Floor Jack with Dual Pistons Quick Lift Pump
products.verdict: A 3-ton low-profile jack with a dual-piston pump and long reach for under $100, one of the best rated here. The listing doesn't give the lift range, so measure your car's jack points first.
products.skip_if: You need to know the lift range before buying; it isn't listed.

products.name: AV Steel Low Profile Floor Jack 2.5 Ton (5000 lbs), Lift Range 3.4" to 14.6" for Cars & Sedans (AV-250102F)
products.verdict: A low-profile car jack whose listing tells you plainly what it isn't for (trucks, SUVs, lifted vehicles) and to check you need no more than 14.6 inches of lift. 1-year warranty.
products.skip_if: You'll ever lift an SUV or truck.
cons: About $22 more than the similar VEVOR

products.name: LARBANKE 3 Ton Hydraulic Floor Jack, 6600 LBS, Lift Range 5.31"-18.11" (S460-X)
products.verdict: A 3-ton carbon-steel jack with an 18-inch lift, padded saddle and handle, and steel casters, and at 46 lbs it's the lightest of the 3-ton jacks here that list a weight.
products.skip_if: Your car sits lower than 5.3 inches at the jack point.
cons: Pump type and warranty not listed

products.name: AV Steel 3 Ton Floor Jack (6000 lbs), Single Piston, Lift Range 5.5" to 18.5" (AV-300101F)
products.verdict: A heavy 63.8 lb steel jack for cars, SUVs, minivans and standard pickups, meeting ANSI/ASME PASE, with a note recommending a jack-point adapter for EVs.
products.skip_if: You want faster lifting; AV Steel's dual-piston model is $3 more.

products.name: VEVOR 3 Ton Low Profile Floor Jack, Dual Pump, 3.35"-19.69" (K500)

specs.pump: Dual piston (7 strokes to full height)

products.verdict: A full-size low-profile 3-ton with a dual pump that reaches full height in 7 strokes and a 52-inch handle for leverage, certified to ASME PALD.
products.best_for: Frequent lifting of everything from low cars to SUVs.
products.skip_if: You'll carry it around; it weighs 73 lbs.

products.name: Jack Boss 3 Ton Low Profile Aluminum and Steel Racing Floor Jack with Dual Pistons, 3-15/16" to 18-5/16" (AS830011L)
products.verdict: An aluminum-and-steel racing jack, each one factory tested to 1.5 times its 3-ton rating, with a dual-piston pump, an 18-inch lift and the ANSI/ASME PASE standard.
products.best_for: Track days and anyone who moves the jack around a lot.
products.skip_if: It stays in one garage; a steel jack lifts the same for less.

avoid.name: TONDA Floor Jack, 3,800 lb Hydraulic Car Jack, 4.9"-11.8"
avoid.verdict: A small jack with an unclear rating and too little lift for most vehicles. For $6 more, the DNA Motoring 2-ton has a clear rating, lifts higher and rates better.
reasons: The title and bullets rate it at 3,800 lb, but the spec table says 2 tons (4,000 lb). On a lifting tool, the capacity is the one number that has to be right.
It tops out at 11.8 inches, the lowest of any jack we compared. That's not enough to get a tire off the ground on most SUVs and trucks, and barely enough to fit a jack stand under many cars.
At 3.8 stars it's the lowest-rated floor jack we looked at.

buyers_guide.q: What capacity floor jack do I need?
buyers_guide.a: A floor jack lifts one end or corner, so it carries well under the vehicle's full weight. A 2-ton jack covers most cars; 3-ton gives margin for SUVs, minivans and pickups. Check the curb weight and pick a jack rated at least three-quarters of it.

Measure from the ground to your car's jack point. Low-profile jacks start around 3 to 3.5 inches for sports cars and lowered sedans. SUVs and trucks need a jack that lifts 18 inches or more so you can fit a stand under them.
A dual-piston pump moves more fluid per stroke, so the saddle rises to the car in a few pumps instead of a dozen. It doesn't add capacity, just speed.

buyers_guide.q: Can I work under a car on a floor jack?
buyers_guide.a: No. Hydraulic jacks can leak down or slip. Lift the car, set jack stands under the manufacturer's support points, lower the car onto the stands, and only then get under it.
Aluminum jacks weigh less to carry around but cost more. Steel jacks are heavier and cheaper and do the same job in a home garage.
